title: Project 02 · Milestone 5 — training that actually converges
statement:
Python Engineer · Project

Milestone 5 — training that actually converges

- DataLoader(dataset, batch_size, shuffle, seed) — deterministic under a seed,

yields batches lazily (module 06).

- A Trainer running the loop with callbacks (on_epoch_end, early stopping).

- Acceptance: train an MLP on XOR to > 99% accuracy in under 2000 epochs, and on a

synthetic 3-class spiral to > 90%.

- Gradient checking: a gradcheck(f, inputs, eps=1e-6) helper comparing analytic

gradients to central finite differences. Every op you write must pass it.

Build in small increments

  1. List the public interfaces and invariants required by this milestone.
  2. Implement one behavior and write a small test in a test_learner.py file.
  3. Run your tests, then run the required milestone checks.
  4. Record a tradeoff and failure case in Notes before moving on.
Hint

Keep dependencies injectable. Prefer in-memory stores, fake clocks, and scripted clients so behavior is reproducible offline. Use the traceback to find the first missing behavior.

Complete project specification

Project 02 — tensorlab: build your own PyTorch

Write a reverse-mode automatic differentiation engine and a neural network framework on

top of it. Pure Python + the standard library for milestones 1–5; numpy is allowed (and

sensible) from milestone 6.

This is the best project in the course for *understanding*: by the end, backpropagation

stops being a black box permanently.

Modules it draws on: 01 (numerics), 04b (dunder methods — the entire operator surface),

06 (generators, topological iteration), 12 (descriptors and registries for Module),

13 (performance).

Milestone 1 — the scalar autograd engine

A Value wrapping a single float, recording the graph as you compute.

from tensorlab import Value

a = Value(2.0)
b = Value(-3.0)
c = a * b + a**2        # builds a DAG
c.backward()
a.grad, b.grad          # dc/da = -3 + 2*2 = 1.0 ; dc/db = 2.0

Required:

- Value(data, label="") with .data, .grad (starts 0.0), ._prev, ._op.

- Operators: + - * / ** - and the reflected forms, so 2 * a and 1 - a work.

Mixing with plain ints/floats is automatic (wrap them).

- .relu(), .tanh(), .exp(), .log(), .sigmoid().

- .backward() does a topological sort of the graph, then applies the chain rule

in reverse. Gradients accumulate (+=), which is what makes a node used twice

(a*a) come out right.

- repr(v) == "Value(data=2.0, grad=0.0)".

- Comparisons by .data, so sorted(values) works.

The single most common bug: = instead of += on .grad. The tests check a*a

specifically for that reason.

Milestone 2 — a tensor

An N-dimensional array with broadcasting, still autograd-aware.

- Tensor(data, requires_grad=False) from nested lists; .shape, .ndim, .size, .dtype.

- Element-wise + - * / with broadcasting (numpy rules), @ for matmul.

- Reductions: .sum(axis=None, keepdims=False), .mean(), .max(), .min().

- Shape ops: .reshape(), .transpose()/.T, .__getitem__ with ints and slices.

- .backward() on a scalar-valued tensor, with correct gradient unbroadcasting

(sum over the broadcast axes when propagating back). This is the hard part.

- .zero_grad(), .detach(), and a no_grad() context manager.

Milestone 3 — the Module system

class MLP(Module):
    def __init__(self, sizes: list[int]) -> None:
        super().__init__()
        self.layers = ModuleList([Linear(a, b) for a, b in itertools.pairwise(sizes)])

    def forward(self, x: Tensor) -> Tensor:
        for i, layer in enumerate(self.layers):
            x = layer(x)
            if i < len(self.layers) - 1:
                x = relu(x)
        return x

- Module.__call__ delegates to .forward (module 04b).

- __setattr__ auto-registers Parameters and child Modules (module 12) so

.parameters() walks the whole tree recursively.

- .named_parameters(), .zero_grad(), .train()/.eval() with a .training flag.

- .state_dict() / .load_state_dict() round-trip through JSON.

- Layers: Linear (with Kaiming init), Sequential, ModuleList, Dropout

(a no-op in eval mode), LayerNorm, Embedding.

Milestone 4 — losses and optimisers

- mse_loss, cross_entropy, binary_cross_entropy — numerically stable

(use log-sum-exp; the tests feed you logits of ±100).

- Optimizer base with .step() / .zero_grad(); implement SGD (with momentum,

weight decay and Nesterov) and Adam (with bias correction).

- lr_scheduler.StepLR and CosineAnnealingLR.

Milestone 5 — training that actually converges

- DataLoader(dataset, batch_size, shuffle, seed) — deterministic under a seed,

yields batches lazily (module 06).

- A Trainer running the loop with callbacks (on_epoch_end, early stopping).

- Acceptance: train an MLP on XOR to > 99% accuracy in under 2000 epochs, and on a

synthetic 3-class spiral to > 90%.

- Gradient checking: a gradcheck(f, inputs, eps=1e-6) helper comparing analytic

gradients to central finite differences. Every op you write must pass it.

Milestone 6 — performance

- Add a numpy backend behind the same API; keep the pure-Python one and pick via

tensorlab.set_backend("numpy" | "python").

- Benchmark a 3-layer MLP forward+backward at batch 256 on both. Expect ~100×.

- Profile the pure-Python path (module 13) and write down where the time actually went.

- Optional: operator fusion, in-place ops, or a @jit-style graph cache.

Going further

- A transformer block: multi-head attention, positional encoding, and train a character

language model on a text file.

- torch.compile-style graph capture, or a simple kernel-fusion pass.

- CUDA via CuPy behind the same backend switch.

- Export to ONNX, or import PyTorch weights and match its outputs to 1e-5.

What "done" means

pytest projects/02_tensorlab is green, gradcheck passes for every op, XOR converges,

and you can explain — out loud, without notes — why gradients must accumulate and what

unbroadcasting is doing.

No complete worked solution is provided. Passing checks verifies this milestone’s executable contract; deployment and optional extensions are ungraded.

App check interfaces & required scenarios

These tests define the concrete interfaces used in this app. Read them before choosing file names and method signatures.

test_acceptance.py

"""Acceptance tests for tensorlab, milestone 1 (the scalar engine).

Run: pytest projects/02_tensorlab -o addopts=""

Later milestones get their own tests — write them yourself as you go. These are the floor.
"""

import math
import sys
from pathlib import Path

import pytest

sys.path.insert(0, str(Path(__file__).parent / "src"))

tensorlab = pytest.importorskip("tensorlab")
Value = tensorlab.Value


class TestForward:
    def test_construction(self):
        v = Value(2.0)
        assert v.data == 2.0
        assert v.grad == 0.0

    def test_int_is_coerced_to_float(self):
        assert isinstance(Value(2).data, float)

    def test_arithmetic(self):
        a, b = Value(2.0), Value(-3.0)
        assert (a + b).data == -1.0
        assert (a * b).data == -6.0
        assert (a - b).data == 5.0
        assert (a / b).data == pytest.approx(-2 / 3)
        assert (a**3).data == 8.0
        assert (-a).data == -2.0

    def test_mixing_with_plain_numbers(self):
        a = Value(2.0)
        assert (a + 1).data == 3.0
        assert (1 + a).data == 3.0
        assert (2 * a).data == 4.0
        assert (1 - a).data == -1.0
        assert (4 / a).data == 2.0

    def test_activations(self):
        assert Value(-2.0).relu().data == 0.0
        assert Value(3.0).relu().data == 3.0
        assert Value(0.0).tanh().data == 0.0
        assert Value(1.0).exp().data == pytest.approx(math.e)
        assert Value(math.e).log().data == pytest.approx(1.0)
        assert Value(0.0).sigmoid().data == pytest.approx(0.5)

    def test_log_of_nonpositive_raises(self):
        with pytest.raises(ValueError):
            Value(0.0).log()

    def test_repr(self):
        assert repr(Value(2.0)) == "Value(data=2.0, grad=0.0)"

    def test_ordering(self):
        assert sorted([Value(3), Value(1)], key=lambda v: v.data)[0].data == 1.0
        assert Value(1) < Value(2)


class TestBackward:
    def test_simple_chain(self):
        a, b = Value(2.0), Value(-3.0)
        c = a * b + a**2
        c.backward()
        assert a.grad == pytest.approx(-3.0 + 2 * 2.0)
        assert b.grad == pytest.approx(2.0)

    def test_gradients_accumulate_for_reused_nodes(self):
        # The classic bug: `=` instead of `+=` gives 2.0 here instead of 4.0.
        a = Value(2.0)
        (a * a).backward()
        assert a.grad == pytest.approx(4.0)

    def test_reuse_across_a_deeper_graph(self):
        a = Value(3.0)
        b = a + a + a  # db/da = 3
        b.backward()
        assert a.grad == pytest.approx(3.0)

    def test_relu_gradient_is_gated(self):
        positive, negative = Value(2.0), Value(-2.0)
        positive.relu().backward()
        negative.relu().backward()
        assert positive.grad == 1.0
        assert negative.grad == 0.0

    def test_tanh_gradient(self):
        x = Value(0.5)
        x.tanh().backward()
        assert x.grad == pytest.approx(1 - math.tanh(0.5) ** 2)

    def test_exp_gradient(self):
        x = Value(1.5)
        x.exp().backward()
        assert x.grad == pytest.approx(math.exp(1.5))

    def test_sigmoid_gradient(self):
        x = Value(0.3)
        x.sigmoid().backward()
        s = 1 / (1 + math.exp(-0.3))
        assert x.grad == pytest.approx(s * (1 - s))

    def test_division_gradient(self):
        a, b = Value(6.0), Value(3.0)
        (a / b).backward()
        assert a.grad == pytest.approx(1 / 3)
        assert b.grad == pytest.approx(-6 / 9)

    def test_power_gradient(self):
        x = Value(3.0)
        (x**4).backward()
        assert x.grad == pytest.approx(4 * 3.0**3)

    def test_a_small_network(self):
        x1, x2 = Value(2.0), Value(0.0)
        w1, w2 = Value(-3.0), Value(1.0)
        bias = Value(6.8813735870195432)
        out = (x1 * w1 + x2 * w2 + bias).tanh()
        out.backward()
        assert out.data == pytest.approx(0.7071, abs=1e-4)
        assert x1.grad == pytest.approx(-1.5, abs=1e-3)
        assert w1.grad == pytest.approx(1.0, abs=1e-3)

    def test_deep_graph_does_not_blow_the_stack(self):
        # An iterative topological sort survives this; naive recursion does not.
        v = Value(1.0)
        acc = v
        for _ in range(5000):
            acc = acc + 1
        acc.backward()
        assert v.grad == pytest.approx(1.0)

    def test_zero_grad(self):
        a = Value(2.0)
        c = a * a
        c.backward()
        c.zero_grad()
        assert a.grad == 0.0 and c.grad == 0.0


class TestGradcheck:
    def test_passes_for_a_correct_graph(self):
        def f(a, b):
            return (a * b + a.tanh()) * b

        inputs = [Value(0.7), Value(-1.3)]
        assert tensorlab.engine.gradcheck(f, inputs) is True

    def test_polynomial(self):
        assert tensorlab.engine.gradcheck(lambda x: x**3 + 2 * x, [Value(1.7)]) is True

    def test_activation_chain(self):
        def f(x):
            return x.sigmoid().log() * x.relu()

        assert tensorlab.engine.gradcheck(f, [Value(1.2)]) is True

test_milestones.py

"""Python Engineer tensorlab contracts. See test bodies for the app-facing APIs."""
import importlib
import json
import math
import random
import pytest


def api():
    return importlib.import_module('tensorlab')


class TestMilestone2:
    def test_shapes_broadcast_and_gradient(self):
        t = api()
        x = t.Tensor([[1.,2.],[3.,4.]], requires_grad=True)
        b = t.Tensor([10.,20.], requires_grad=True)
        assert tuple(x.shape)==(2,2) and x.ndim==2 and x.size==4
        y=(x+b).sum(); y.backward()
        assert b.grad.tolist()==[2.,2.]
        assert x.grad.tolist()==[[1.,1.],[1.,1.]]
        assert x.T.tolist()==[[1.,3.],[2.,4.]]
        assert x.reshape(4).tolist()==[1.,2.,3.,4.]

    def test_matmul_and_detach(self):
        t=api();x=t.Tensor([[1.,2.]],requires_grad=True)
        assert (x@t.Tensor([[3.],[4.]])).tolist()==[[11.]]
        assert x.detach().requires_grad is False
        with t.no_grad(): assert (x+x).requires_grad is False


class TestMilestone3:
    def test_parameters_state_and_eval(self):
        t=api();layer=t.Linear(2,3)
        parameters=list(layer.parameters())
        assert parameters and all(p.requires_grad for p in parameters)
        assert tuple(layer(t.Tensor([[1.,2.]])).shape)==(1,3)
        state=json.loads(json.dumps(layer.state_dict()))
        other=t.Linear(2,3);other.load_state_dict(state)
        assert other.state_dict()==state
        model=t.Sequential(layer,t.Dropout(0.5));model.eval()
        assert model.training is False and layer.training is False
        assert model(t.Tensor([[1.,2.]])).tolist()==model(t.Tensor([[1.,2.]])).tolist()

    def test_embedding_and_normalization(self):
        t=api();embedded=t.Embedding(4,3)(t.Tensor([0,2]))
        assert tuple(embedded.shape)==(2,3)
        values=t.LayerNorm(3)(t.Tensor([[1.,2.,3.]]))
        assert abs(sum(values.tolist()[0]))<1e-5


class TestMilestone4:
    def test_losses_are_finite_and_correct(self):
        t=api()
        assert t.mse_loss(t.Tensor([1.,3.]),t.Tensor([2.,2.])).item()==pytest.approx(1.)
        value=t.cross_entropy(t.Tensor([[100.,-100.]]),t.Tensor([0])).item()
        assert math.isfinite(value) and value<1e-5
        assert math.isfinite(t.binary_cross_entropy(t.Tensor([0.2,0.8]),t.Tensor([0.,1.])).item())

    @pytest.mark.parametrize('name',['SGD','Adam'])
    def test_optimizer_decreases_loss(self,name):
        t=api();p=t.Parameter([3.]);opt=getattr(t,name)([p],lr=0.05)
        before=(p*p).sum().item()
        for _ in range(10):
            opt.zero_grad();(p*p).sum().backward();opt.step()
        assert (p*p).sum().item()<before

    def test_scheduler(self):
        t=api();opt=t.SGD([t.Parameter([1.])],lr=1.)
        scheduler=t.lr_scheduler.StepLR(opt,step_size=1,gamma=0.5);scheduler.step()
        assert opt.lr==pytest.approx(0.5)


class TestMilestone5:
    def test_loader_is_reproducible_and_gradcheck(self):
        t=api();data=list(range(11))
        a=list(t.DataLoader(data,batch_size=3,shuffle=True,seed=7))
        b=list(t.DataLoader(data,batch_size=3,shuffle=True,seed=7))
        assert a==b and sorted(x for batch in a for x in batch)==data
        assert t.gradcheck(lambda x:(x*x).sum(),[t.Tensor([1.,2.],requires_grad=True)])

    def test_xor_training_contract(self):
        t=api();random.seed(7)
        model=t.Sequential(t.Linear(2,8),t.Tanh(),t.Linear(8,1),t.Sigmoid())
        optimizer=t.Adam(list(model.parameters()),lr=0.05)
        callbacks=[]
        trainer=t.Trainer(model,optimizer=optimizer,loss=t.binary_cross_entropy)
        x=t.Tensor([[0.,0.],[0.,1.],[1.,0.],[1.,1.]])
        target=t.Tensor([[0.],[1.],[1.],[0.]])
        trainer.fit(x,target,max_epochs=2000,on_epoch_end=lambda epoch,loss:callbacks.append(loss))
        predictions=[float(row[0])>=0.5 for row in model(x).tolist()]
        assert predictions==[False,True,True,False]
        assert callbacks and len(callbacks)<=2000



class TestMilestone6:
    def test_backends_agree_for_values_and_gradients(self):
        t=api();outputs=[]
        try:
            for backend in ['python','numpy']:
                t.set_backend(backend)
                x=t.Tensor([[1.,2.],[3.,4.]],requires_grad=True)
                y=(x*x).sum();y.backward();outputs.append((y.item(),x.grad.tolist()))
            assert outputs[0]==outputs[1]
        finally: t.set_backend('python')

    @pytest.mark.benchmark
    def test_backend_benchmark(self):
        import time
        t=api()
        for backend in ['python','numpy']:
            t.set_backend(backend);x=t.Tensor([[1.]*16 for _ in range(256)],requires_grad=True)
            start=time.perf_counter();(x*x).sum().backward()
            print(backend,time.perf_counter()-start)
        t.set_backend('python')
